correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge2\), \(\rho>0\), and \(B>0\), a connected-graph energy argument proves positive definiteness on the entire gain simplex. The second directional derivative of \(\operatorname{tr}(QA^{-1})\) is strictly positive in every nonzero diagonal direction because \(Q\) is positive definite. The unique optimizer is therefore leaf-symmetric without an a priori symmetry assumption. Schur inversion gives the reduced cost exactly, and both endpoint derivative identities were independently symbolically checked. Strict convexity converts the sign at the zero-hub boundary into a necessary and sufficient condition, while \(F'(B)=(B+2)/B>0\) prevents zero leaf gains. The support envelope is unimodal with its unique critical root \(z=(\sqrt5-1)/2\) and value \((5\sqrt5-11)/2\). Endpoint expansions prove the two asymptotic laws. The submitted verification program ran 3,371 finite exact and numerical assertions; those do not replace the universal analytical proof.

value.rationale: The freely allocated noise-suppression problem on a star exposes a nontrivial noise-strength/budget bifurcation: despite maximal degree, the hub is exactly unpinned on an interval that re-closes to one point at a universal golden-ratio cusp. The full two-parameter theorem determines every allocation, includes a path on three vertices exhibiting the effect, and shows distinct \(O(m^{-1})\) versus \(O(m^2)\) switching-budget scales. The motivating question is how unequal disturbance power should alter optimal network feedback, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Its weighted-noise structural phase diagram is not merely the already known homogeneous-noise subcase.
